_doc: Per-MAC energy models e(b,t) in pJ, beta=b-t (effective width). kind=poly: a0+a1*beta+a2*beta^2+aE*2^beta+mu*b; dvafs: (a0+a2*beta^2)*(V(beta)/V(8))^2 with V=v0+v1*beta/8; family: e8*[phi+(1-phi)*g(beta)/g(8)]; flat: e8. All models give e(8,0) close to 0.3 pJ so absolute scales are comparable; conclusions depend only on energy ratios (Proposition 4).

H0.name: Bit-parallel array MAC, fixed 32-bit accumulator (45 nm; main text)
H0.basis: Horowitz (2014): 8-bit mult 0.2 pJ, 32-bit add 0.1 pJ; multiplier energy quadratic in width

H1.name: Array MAC, precision-scaled accumulator
H1.basis: accumulator width 2*beta+10 bits, adder energy linear in width (0.1 pJ per 32 bits)

H2.name: Bit-serial datapath
H2.basis: Stripes/UNPU-style: energy proportional to the number of serial bit cycles; e(8)=0.3 pJ

H3.name: Memory-augmented (operand fetch)
H3.basis: R1 model: H0 + 0.15 pJ per operand bit fetched; truncation does not reduce fetch energy

H4.name: Voltage-accuracy-scaled array MAC (DVAFS-like)
H4.basis: supply lowered linearly from 1.0 V at 8 bits towards 0.6 V as the critical path shortens; dynamic energy ~ V^2

H5.name: Analog in-memory MAC, ADC-dominated
H5.basis: ADC energy doubles per bit of resolution (Walden figure of merit); fixed array/periphery share 10% at 8 bits

H6.name: Fixed-width INT8 SIMD datapath (CPU/MCU/GPU lanes)
H6.basis: sub-8-bit operands occupy full 8-bit lanes; no arithmetic saving below 8 bits
